Thanks Marissa — appreciated the recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Usage profile: our forecast today is 100M–300M tokens / month for the first 6 months, ramping toward the high end if the pilot looks good. ~85% generation, 15% embeddings.
- Budget: target $5k–$15k / month depending on traffic (so your $50 / 1M tokens target maps cleanly: 100M * $50 = $5k, 300M * $50 = $15k).
- Pricing expectation: BrightCart expects the invoice from AWS Marketplace to show the per-1M token price. We’d prefer buyer-facing price to be $50 / 1M tokens. Ideally Redwood nets ~ $50 after any marketplace fees are applied, but procurement usually cares about the buyer-facing price.

- Do you support per-1M token metering on AWS private offers (one SKU) versus multiple SKUs? We prefer one SKU to simplify invoicing.

Marissa / Rafael — doing a quick math pass on buyer-facing vs seller-net pricing for the private offer. See summary below (pulled from the attached workbook). I’ll paste the core logic here so we can share a short table with the customer and AWS: 

Assumptions:
- Target buyer-facing price (P_buyer) that BrightCart wants = $50 / 1M tokens
- Marketplace fee (F) is charged as a % of the buyer-facing price (common for AWS) — we need confirmation on the exact % (typical 10%–12% ranges).

If buyer pays P_buyer and marketplace fee is F, Redwood net (P_net) = P_buyer * (1 - F)
If Redwood wants P_net to be $50, then buyer-facing price must be P_buyer = P_net / (1 - F)

Examples:
- If F = 10% -> P_net = $50 when P_buyer = $50 / (1 - 0.10) = $55.56 (buyer pays $55.56; Redwood nets ~$50)
- If F = 12% -> P_buyer = $56.82
- If Redwood sets P_buyer = $50 and F = 10%, Redwood nets $45 (not $50).

Operational notes for private offers on AWS:
- AWS supports metering-based products; we can expose a single per-1M-token usage SKU so BrightCart sees one line item.
- Private offers can set the buyer-facing per-unit price. The marketplace fee is taken out of the payout to the seller unless the seller chooses to bake fee into the listed price.
- Doc/contract flow: need AWS private-offer listing id and a few administrative fields (seller account, offer term, start/end dates). Priya — if you can confirm fee %, we can finalize recommended list prices in the workbook.

I’ve attached the same redwood_pricing_model.xlsx with the examples populated for F = 8%, 10%, 12% and buyer-facing price vs seller-net columns.

Aditya

Hi Marissa / Tom — thanks, and great to meet you on the call. A few quick clarifications from the AWS Marketplace side: 

1) Fee: For SaaS metered products the standard AWS Marketplace transaction fee is 10% on buyer-facing list price for private offers unless otherwise negotiated with Marketplace Sales. The buyer-facing invoice will show the line item(s) at the listed price; fee is taken out during payout reconciliation. If you want Redwood to net $50 / 1M, your buyer-facing price should be ~$55.56 (50 / 0.90).

2) Metering: AWS supports a single metered usage SKU for per-1M token metering. You can expose a single usage dimension (e.g., "1M_token_unit") and report usage in units. That will show as one line item on buyer invoices.

3) Private offer flow: we need the seller listing id, your proposed buyer-facing unit price(s), and the term length. I’ve attached the AWS_Private_Offer_Checklist.pdf and a link to the private offers guide: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/marketplace/latest/userguide/private-offers.html

4) Timeline: once we receive the listing id and the proposed offer (price + term), typical private offer activation for an established partner takes ~3–5 business days (assuming no legal changes). If you need custom fee arrangements, that can extend the timeline.

Next step suggested: Marissa / Aditya send the final proposed buyer-facing price(s) (we recommend providing two options: buyer-facing price that results in Redwood netting $50 and a buyer-facing price that is $50 so BrightCart can choose which number matters more to procurement). Also include preferred SKU name for metering. I’ll kick off the private offer creation with Marketplace Sales once we have the listing id and prices.

Best,
Priya Singh
